questions.question: Explain the principle and procedure of Bradford's method of protein determination
questions.solution_html:
• . The assay relies on the binding of a dye called Coomassie Brilliant Blue G-250 to proteins. Under
  • highly acidic conditions, the dye is naturally in a doubly protonated red/brown state. When the dye
  • binds to proteins, it converts into a stable blue, unprotonated form. This blue protein-dye complex
  • shows maximum absorbance at 595 nm. The increase in absorbance at 595 nm is directly proportional
  • to the amount of protein present. Add 1 mL of the sample to a test tube. To control tube add 1 ml
  • distilled water. To both tubes, add 1 ml of Bradford reagent. Mix the contents and keep it aside for 10
  • minutes. Observe the colour change and take the reading using a spectrophotometer at 595 nm with
  • control tube as blank
questions.final_answer: control tube as blank
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain Hager's test and Mayer's test for the detection of alkaloids
questions.solution_html:
• Mayers Test- Nitrogen atoms in basic alkaloids form coordinate bonds or insoluble complexes with
  • potassium-mercuric ions. This results in the formation of a cream-colored or pale yellow precipitate.
  • Take 2 ml of a given sample in a clean, dry test tube. Add 2 ml of concentrated HCl to both the tubes
  • and mix them. Add 5 drops of Mayer’s Reagent. The emergence of a white precipitate or a distinct
  • green coloration serves as a positive confirmation for the presence of alkaloid compounds.
  • Hager’s Test- Picric acid acts as an organic acid that forms crystalline picrate salts with basic alkaloid
  • molecules. Take 2 ml of a given sample in a clean, dry test tube. Add 6 drops of Hagers's Reagent. Mix
  • well. The formation of an yellow precipitate indicate the presence of alkaloids
questions.final_answer: well. The formation of an yellow precipitate indicate the presence of alkaloids

questions.question: What is solvent-solvent extraction? Explain co-current method.
questions.solution_html:
• the crude plant extract dissolved in a solvent is treated with another pure immiscible solvent. This helps
  • to transfer the compound on interest or the impurities into the fresh immiscible solvent. In a co-current
  • (or forward-flow) solvent-solvent extraction mechanism, the feed solution
  • metabolite) and the immiscible extracting solvent travel through the extraction system in the same
  • direction. It is useful for fast, equilibrium-limited, or reactive extractions where prolonged contact is
  • undesirable. The mechanism relies on a repeating cycle of stages. Each stage consists of two distinct
  • physical phases: Mixing (Mass Transfer) and Settling (Phase Separation).
questions.final_answer: physical phases: Mixing (Mass Transfer) and Settling (Phase Separation)

questions.question: Explain IR spectrophotometer
questions.solution_html:
• an analytical instrument that measures how a chemical sample absorbs infrared light to identify
  • functional groups and determine molecular structures. Infrared Source: Generates broad-spectrum IR
  • radiation using heated elements like a Nernst glower, or nichrome coils. Sample Compartment: Holds
  • solid, liquid, or gas cells. Monochromator - Dispersive instruments use prisms or diffraction grating.
  • Fourier transform IR (FTIR) instruments use a Michelson interferometer. Detector: Converts optical
  • signals into electrical signals using thermal. Recorder Processor: Plots transmittance or absorbance
  • (y-axis) against wavenumber or wavelength (x-axis)
questions.final_answer: (y-axis) against wavenumber or wavelength (x-axis)

questions.question: Write an essay on Ultrasound assisted extraction and Super Critical Fluid extraction
questions.solution_html:
• Ultrasound assisted extraction- Ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) is a green, non-thermal technique
  • that uses high-frequency, high-intensity sound waves to recover valuable secondary plant metabolites
  • (such as phenolics, flavonoids, alkaloids, and essential oils) from plant matrices. Principle- Acoustic
  • Cavitation. Bubble Formation: Low-frequency ultrasound waves (typically 20 kHz to several MHz)
  • pass through a liquid solvent containing immersed plant material. Cavitation: The pressure cycles create
  • microscopic vacuum bubbles that grow and violently collapse. Cell Disruption: The collapse generates
  • localized high temperatures, high pressures, and intense shear forces. These forces break plant cell
  • walls and membranes, accelerating the release of intracellular metabolites into the solvent
  • Super Critical Fluid extraction- separation technique that uses a fluid in a supercritical state (meaning
  • it is kept at a temperature and pressure above its critical point where liquid and gas phases merge) —to
  • dissolve and isolate specific target compounds from a solid or liquid matrix. A gas like carbon dioxide
  • (CO₂) is pressurized and heated past its critical point, giving it gas-like diffusion properties and liquid
  • like dissolving power (Supercritical fluid). The supercritical fluid flows through a high-pressure vessel
  • holding the raw material to dissolve the desired components. The system reduces pressure in a separator
  • vessel, turning the CO₂ back into a gas so it releases the extracted product for collection.
questions.final_answer: vessel, turning the CO₂ back into a gas so it releases the extracted product for collection
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain vertical gel electrophoresis
questions.solution_html:
• Separation of charged molecules like proteins and short nucleic acid through a vertically placed gel.
  • Gel made of Poly acrylamide (Acrylamide, bis acrylamides, APS and TEMED). Two gels- Resolving
  • gel and stacking gel. Stacking gel (highly porous layer with a pH of 6.8) stack the proteins and resolving
  • gel (dense layer with a higher pH of 8.8) separates protein based on charge and mass. Native PAGE
  • separation based on charge and mass, SDS- separation based on mass only- SDS non-reductive and
  • SDS reductive PAGE. Stacking gel low voltage, for resolving gel, enhance the voltage. Buffer system
  • TAE or TBE buffer. Once tracking dye reaches the end, electrophoresis is stopped and the gel is stained
  • and viewed.
questions.final_answer: and viewed

questions.question: Explain IR spectrophotometer
questions.solution_html:
• an analytical instrument that measures how a chemical sample absorbs infrared light to identify
  • functional groups and determine molecular structures. Infrared Source: Generates broad-spectrum IR
  • radiation using heated elements like a Nernst glower, or nichrome coils. Sample Compartment: Holds
  • solid, liquid, or gas cells. Monochromator - Dispersive instruments use prisms or diffraction grating.
  • Fourier transform IR (FTIR) instruments use a Michelson interferometer. Detector: Converts optical
  • signals into electrical signals using thermal. Recorder Processor: Plots transmittance or absorbance
  • (y-axis) against wavenumber or wavelength (x-axis)

questions.question: Write an essay on Ultrasound assisted extraction and Super Critical Fluid extraction
questions.solution_html:
• Ultrasound assisted extraction- Ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) is a green, non-thermal technique
  • that uses high-frequency, high-intensity sound waves to recover valuable secondary plant metabolites
  • (such as phenolics, flavonoids, alkaloids, and essential oils) from plant matrices. Principle- Acoustic
  • Cavitation. Bubble Formation: Low-frequency ultrasound waves (typically 20 kHz to several MHz)
  • pass through a liquid solvent containing immersed plant material. Cavitation: The pressure cycles create
  • microscopic vacuum bubbles that grow and violently collapse. Cell Disruption: The collapse generates
  • localized high temperatures, high pressures, and intense shear forces. These forces break plant cell
  • walls and membranes, accelerating the release of intracellular metabolites into the solvent
  • Super Critical Fluid extraction- separation technique that uses a fluid in a supercritical state (meaning
  • it is kept at a temperature and pressure above its critical point where liquid and gas phases merge) —to
  • dissolve and isolate specific target compounds from a solid or liquid matrix. A gas like carbon dioxide
  • (CO₂) is pressurized and heated past its critical point, giving it gas-like diffusion properties and liquid
  • like dissolving power (Supercritical fluid). The supercritical fluid flows through a high-pressure vessel
  • holding the raw material to dissolve the desired components. The system reduces pressure in a separator
  • vessel, turning the CO₂ back into a gas so it releases the extracted product for collection.
questions.final_answer: vessel, turning the CO₂ back into a gas so it releases the extracted product for collection

questions.question: Explain vertical gel electrophoresis
questions.solution_html:
• Separation of charged molecules like proteins and short nucleic acid through a vertically placed gel.
  • Gel made of Poly acrylamide (Acrylamide, bis acrylamides, APS and TEMED). Two gels- Resolving
  • gel and stacking gel. Stacking gel (highly porous layer with a pH of 6.8) stack the proteins and resolving
  • gel (dense layer with a higher pH of 8.8) separates protein based on charge and mass. Native PAGE
  • separation based on charge and mass, SDS- separation based on mass only- SDS non-reductive and
  • SDS reductive PAGE. Stacking gel low voltage, for resolving gel, enhance the voltage. Buffer system
  • TAE or TBE buffer. Once tracking dye reaches the end, electrophoresis is stopped and the gel is stained
  • and viewed.
